layers.note: The prostrate alpine form: a low, spreading evergreen mat on rocky, open ground in the meadows and above tree line.

moisture.note: Dry to moderately moist, rocky, well-drained ground.

heat_load.note: Open, exposed ground of any aspect, often sunny ridges and rock.

elevation_m.note: Sea level in the far north to about 3,400 m in California and 3,955 m in Wyoming (FEIS, Tirmenstein 1999, which lists 1,373 to 3,955 m across four western states).

shade_tolerance.note: Shade intolerant; usually in open places (FEIS, Tirmenstein 1999).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −30 to 6 °C; gone below −40 °C and above 10 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −50 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −60 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 6 to 22 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 500 to 5,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 150 to 3,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.2, gone by 0.1.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.7 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.85.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Common juniper is circumboreal, across North America, Europe, northern Asia and Japan, and widespread beyond the northern limit of trees (FEIS, Tirmenstein 1999). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
